budget_items.what_was_said: The board reviewed and signed a motor vehicle and trailer excise commitment; discussion was over whether a vote was needed versus just signing.

An applicant's Chapter 61A filing came with a check for the registry; the board agreed their signature would suffice, pending notarization since it is a lien.

budget_items.topic: CI dynamic mapping / additional public-facing layers
budget_items.what_was_said: The GIS vendor could configure additional public-facing map layers such as neighborhood boundaries, but this would be an added fee beyond current services.

budget_items.topic: Photo and document uploads via GIS vendor
budget_items.what_was_said: Years ago the vendor quoted a per-photo charge to add property photos; the board believes the document-upload feature they already pay for could be used to attach photos and sketches instead.

budget_items.topic: CI/GIS vendor contract and fee schedule
budget_items.what_was_said: The only contract copy on hand dates to 2020; the board wants an updated fee schedule to know the cost of each available feature before the next vendor meeting.

decisions.decision: An office staff member (Denise) will staff an informational booth at next Tuesday's town hall meet-and-greet on exemptions/abatements/deferrals/tax workoffs; board members' own availability was still unconfirmed.
The finance director will look into whether supplemental tax bills have gone out and report back at the next meeting.
The board's signature will serve as the vote to approve the agricultural Chapter 61A exemption filing, once notarized.
The chair will ask the GIS vendor (CI) for an updated, written fee schedule ahead of the May 12 vendor meeting.

The consultant will aim to have the problematic lake-area neighborhood (currently lumped into one oversized neighborhood) reclassified in time for the December tax bill, though this was called an aggressive, non-guaranteed target.
The website's exemptions page title will be changed to also reference deferrals, to make it easier for residents to find, to be handled by the town's web team (Cara/Carara) by the next day.

minutes.headline: Assessors push GIS vendor for a fee schedule while racing to fix lakefront neighborhoods by December bills
minutes.summary:
The Board of Assessors met mainly to prepare for redoing property "neighborhoods" townwide under a state DOR directive, starting with long-disputed lakefront classifications, and to review what their GIS vendor (heard as CI/CGI) already provides versus what costs extra. No major votes were taken beyond routine signing of excise commitments and a motion to adjourn into executive session over abatement/exemption matters.</parameter>

what_happened.line: A consultant aims to reclassify the disputed lakefront neighborhood in time for the December tax bill, though called an aggressive, non-guaranteed target.
The board asked its GIS vendor for an updated written fee schedule ahead of a May 12 vendor meeting.
The board signed routine motor vehicle, trailer, and boat excise commitments without a formal vote.
The finance director will check whether supplemental tax bills have gone out and report back next meeting.
The board voted to adjourn into executive session to discuss abatement and exemption matters.

why_it_matters: Homeowners in the lake-area neighborhood could see their property classification, and with it their assessment, change as soon as the December tax bill.
The GIS vendor's fee schedule will determine what the town pays for the mapping tools used to draw and redraw assessment neighborhoods townwide.
Residents waiting on a supplemental tax bill will learn its status once the finance director reports back.
